packageRules.description: The DHI .NET SDK and runtime move together: TargetLatestRuntimePatch makes an app need the runtime patch its SDK knows, so an SDK bump without the matching runtime bump makes the app fail to start, though the image still builds.
A .NET major is due only when the app's upstream retargets, and it then moves with the app's own bump, so it waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard.

DHI's Python runtime and its -dev image move together. An app's venv is built by the -dev image's Python and run by the runtime's, so the two must be the same Python. Renovate opens one pull request for a new tag of both, but one for each image's digest when DHI rebuilds a tag.

Subject prefix for a Python package a repository's own regex manager pins, such as each line of python/pins.txt: the image's locks are generated from those pins, so each is an input of the image's build. A custom manager cannot carry commitMessagePrefix.

Renovate's own Python managers never edit a file under python/, or a test file under a testdata folder. The locks under python/ are generated by the repository's own command, with a sha256 for every file, so an edit of one line would leave a lock out of step with what it was generated from. Their packages move through the pins and the app's own version instead. A requirements file under testdata, such as the sample list the pins tool's tests read, is not installed anywhere, so an update of it changes no image.
